term: 常见物质的俗名与主要成分
termEn: Common Names and What They Really Are
oneLiner: 纯碱不是碱、干冰不是冰、水银不是银：常用俗名与它们的真实成分对照。
oneLinerEn: Soda ash is no base, dry ice is no ice, quicksilver is no silver: the common names beside what they actually are.
detail: 俗名有三个坑。一是分类错位：纯碱 Na₂CO₃、小苏打 NaHCO₃、胆矾 CuSO₄·5H₂O 都是盐，水溶液却有的显碱性，因而被叫成「碱」；二是混合物与纯净物不分：王水是浓盐酸与浓硝酸按体积 3∶1 现配，碱石灰是 NaOH 与 CaO 的混合物，漂白粉的有效成分只是 Ca(ClO)₂，天然气、沼气、坑气都以 CH₄ 为主但不是纯甲烷；三是水合数字被丢掉：写 CuSO₄ 是无色粉末，蓝色晶体是 CuSO₄·5H₂O（胆矾）。另外「主要成分」这个词要谨慎：石灰石与大理石以 CaCO₃ 为主，但含 MgCO₃、SiO₂ 等杂质；石英、水晶、玛瑙与沙子的主要成分都是 SiO₂，区别在晶体颗粒与杂质而不是成分。
detailEn: Three traps hide in these names. First, the class is wrong: Na₂CO₃, NaHCO₃ and CuSO₄·5H₂O are all salts, and the first two are called 'alkali' only because their solutions are basic. Second, mixtures are named as if pure: aqua regia is HCl and HNO₃ in a 3-to-1 volume ratio mixed at the bench, soda lime is NaOH with CaO, bleaching powder works through just its Ca(ClO)₂, and natural, marsh and firedamp are mostly CH₄ but not pure methane. Third, the water of crystallisation gets dropped: anhydrous CuSO₄ is a pale powder, the blue crystals are CuSO₄·5H₂O. And 'mainly' matters — limestone and marble are mostly CaCO₃ with MgCO₃ and SiO₂ along, while quartz, rock crystal, agate and sand are all SiO₂ and differ in crystal size and impurity, not in substance.

term: 常见物质与溶液的颜色
termEn: Colours of Common Substances and Solutions
oneLiner: 固体看亚铁红褐、铜蓝，溶液看铜蓝铁黄、高锰酸紫红：颜色是最快的判断线索。
oneLinerEn: Solids: rust-brown iron(III), blue copper; solutions: blue Cu²⁺, yellow Fe³⁺, purple permanganate — colour is the fastest clue.
detail: 颜色只能当线索不能当结论。同一物质颗粒大小不同颜色就变：块状金是黄色但金粉是黑色，AgCl 白色沉淀见光逐渐转灰紫。溶液的颜色来自水合离子，浓度很浅时几乎看不出，所以「无色的 FeCl₃ 溶液」可能只是太稀。三价铁的水合离子属黄到棕黄，二价铁浅绿，高锰酸根紫红，这三样在实验报告里最容易互认错。气体的两条：Cl₂ 黄绿色、NO₂ 红棕色，其余常见气体无色。沉淀的记忆口诀：白色 CaCO₃、BaSO₄、AgCl、Mg(OH)₂；蓝色 Cu(OH)₂；红褐色 Fe(OH)₃；黄色 AgI、Ag₃PO₄。
detailEn: Colour is a clue, never a verdict. The same substance changes hue with particle size: gold is yellow in lump and black as powder, and white AgCl drifts to grey-violet in light. Solution colour comes from hydrated ions and simply vanishes when dilute, so a 'colourless FeCl₃' may only be a weak one. The three most confused in lab reports are the yellow-brown of iron(III), the pale green of iron(II) and the purple-red of permanganate. Two gases carry colour — chlorine's yellow-green and nitrogen dioxide's red-brown — and the rest are clear. For precipitates: white CaCO₃, BaSO₄, AgCl, Mg(OH)₂; blue Cu(OH)₂; rust-brown Fe(OH)₃; yellow AgI and Ag₃PO₄.

termEn: Solubility Rules for Acids, Bases and Salts
oneLiner: 钾钠铵硝皆可溶，盐酸盐不溶银，硫酸盐不溶钡，碳酸盐只溶钾钠铵。
oneLinerEn: All potassium, sodium, ammonium and nitrate salts dissolve; silver chloride does not; barium sulfate does not; carbonates answer only to K, Na and NH₄.
detail: 口诀只是地图，分界数字才有用：习惯上以 20 ℃ 时在 100 g 水里溶解的质量分级——大于 10 g 易溶，1 到 10 g 可溶，0.01 到 1 g 微溶，小于 0.01 g 难溶。所以上面的「不溶」从来不是真正不溶：BaSO₄ 在 20 ℃ 仍有约每升两毫克的溶解量，刚好落入难溶区。三个常见陷阱：微溶物 Ca(OH)₂ 做澄清石灰水时是溶的、写石灰乳时是悬浊；Ag₂SO₄、CaSO₄ 属微溶，浓度大时一样会浑；MgCO₃ 微溶、Mg(OH)₂ 难溶，所以软化硬水时镁必须先转成氢氧化物才能除净。口诀之外还得记特例：盐酸盐里 Hg₂Cl₂ 也不溶；Fe³⁺、Al³⁺ 根本没有正经的碳酸盐，一遇水就双水解。
detailEn: The rhyme is a map; the numbers are the territory. Custom grades solubility at 20 °C in 100 g of water: over 10 g very soluble, 1 to 10 g soluble, 0.01 to 1 g slight, below 0.01 g poor. So 'insoluble' is never truly so — BaSO₄ still dissolves about two milligrams per litre at 20 °C and just lands in the poor class. Three traps: Ca(OH)₂ is dissolved in clear limewater but a suspension as milk of lime, and which one you mean changes the answer; Ag₂SO₄ and CaSO₄ are merely slight yet turn a flask cloudy when concentrated; MgCO₃ is slight while Mg(OH)₂ is poor, so water softening must convert magnesium to the hydroxide before it is genuinely gone. Past the rhyme, remember the exceptions: Hg₂Cl₂ is also insoluble among chlorides, and iron(III) and aluminium have no real carbonate at all — in water they hydrolyse instead.

termEn: Flame Colours as an Element Test
oneLiner: 钠黄、钾紫、铜绿、钡黄绿：金属离子把火焰染成自己的颜色，烟花也是同一回事。
oneLinerEn: Sodium yellow, potassium violet, copper green, barium yellow-green: ions tint the flame, and fireworks use the same trick.
detail: 焰色反应发光来自电子受热跃迁后回落时放出的光，不生成新物质，中学把它归作物理变化；它检验的是元素本身，所以 NaCl、Na₂SO₄、NaOH 焰色一样黄。操作叫「烧—蘸—烧」：先蘸稀盐酸在氧化焰上烧到火焰无色，再蘸样品灼烧，每换一个样重新处理一次；没有铂丝时用无锈铁丝代替。两个易错点：观察钾的焰色必须透过蓝色钴玻璃，因为那怕微量钠的黄光会把钾的紫色完全盖住；洗铂丝用盐酸而不用硫酸，因为硫酸盐难挥发。钠的黄光灵敏度极高，汗渍、自来水、玻璃里都有，所以上手前先把丝烧干净，否则看到的全是黄。烟花的五种颜色就是五种金属盐：锶盐红、钡盐黄绿、钠盐黄、铜盐蓝绿、镁铝粉白亮。
detailEn: The light comes from electrons raised by the heat and falling back, dropping photons on the way down; no new substance forms, which is why schools file it as a physical change. What is tested is the element itself, so NaCl, Na₂SO₄ and NaOH all burn the same yellow. The drill is 'burn, dip, burn': wet the wire with dilute hydrochloric acid, hold it in the oxidising flame until nothing shows, dip it into the sample, and repeat the whole clean between samples, substituting a rust-free iron wire if platinum is out of reach. Two classic slips: potassium's violet must be viewed through blue cobalt glass, because trace sodium yellow drowns it completely, and the wire is cleaned in hydrochloric not sulfuric acid since sulfate salts refuse to volatilise. Sodium yellow is sensitive to a fault — sweat, tap water and glass all carry it — so burn the wire clean first or every sample will look yellow. Fireworks are just five salts: strontium red, barium yellow-green, sodium yellow, copper blue-green, and magnesium or aluminium powder for white.

subs.name: 银离子（来自 AgNO₃ 溶液）
subs.note: 一碰上 Cl⁻ 就沉淀，但要先酸化，不让 CO₃²⁻ 假阳性。
subs.noteEn: Drops at once with chloride, but acidify first so carbonate cannot fake the result.

subs.name: 氯离子
subs.note: 盐酸与氯化物里都有；氯水氧化亚铁之后留下的也是它。
subs.noteEn: In hydrochloric acid and the chlorides; also what chlorine water leaves after oxidising iron(II).

subs.name: 钡离子（来自 BaCl₂ 溶液）
subs.note: 检验 SO₄²⁻ 用它，酸先下是为了不让碳酸根、亚硫酸根一起浑浊。
subs.noteEn: The reagent for sulfate; the acid goes in first so carbonate and sulfite cannot cloud it too.

subs.name: 硫酸根离子
subs.note: BaSO₄ 不溶于水也不溶于酸，这是它与 CaCO₃ 的分界。
subs.noteEn: BaSO₄ is insoluble in water and in acid, which is where it parts company with CaCO₃.

subs.name: 碳酸根离子
subs.note: 遇酸即放 CO₂，但只能说明「碳酸根或碳酸氢根」，两者还要分开。
subs.noteEn: Acid drives off CO₂, but that only says carbonate or hydrogen carbonate; separating them needs another step.

subs.name: 氢离子（稀盐酸提供）
subs.note: 写离子方程式时 HCl 拆成 H⁺ 与 Cl⁻，水与沉淀不拆。
subs.noteEn: In ionic equations HCl is written apart as H⁺ and Cl⁻; water and precipitates stay whole.

subs.name: 铵根离子
subs.note: 常见阳离子里唯一含氮的，遇碱放氨，氮肥与铵盐都靠它鉴定。
subs.noteEn: The one nitrogen-bearing common cation: base frees its ammonia, which is how ammonium salts are recognised.

subs.name: 氢氧根（浓 NaOH）
subs.note: 要浓、要热，氨才能大量逸出；稀冷时几乎闻不到。
subs.noteEn: Strong and hot, or the ammonia stays in solution and nothing shows.

subs.name: 铁离子（三价）
subs.note: 与 SCN⁻ 生成血红色配合物；也是亚铁被氯水氧化后的产物。
subs.noteEn: Blood-red with thiocyanate, and what chlorine water turns iron(II) into.

subs.name: 硫氰酸根（KSCN 溶液）
subs.note: 极灵敏，痕量 Fe³⁺ 也显色；先不显色本身就能说明没有三价铁。
subs.noteEn: Sensitive to traces; a failure to colour is itself evidence that no iron(III) is there.

subs.name: 亚铁离子（二价）
subs.note: 浅绿，加 KSCN 不变红；被氯水或双氧水氧化后才红，两步连着做才能证明原液含亚铁。
subs.noteEn: Pale green and silent with thiocyanate; it reddens only after chlorine or peroxide has oxidised it, and only the pair of steps proves iron(II).

subs.name: 氯气（氯水）
subs.note: 充当氧化剂，把 Fe²⁺ 拉到 Fe³⁺，自身还原成 Cl⁻。
subs.noteEn: The oxidant: lifts iron(II) up to iron(III) and comes down to chloride.

subs.name: 氯化银（白色凝乳状沉淀）
subs.note: 不溶于稀硝酸，见光逐渐变灰紫。
subs.noteEn: Undissolved by dilute nitric acid; drifts grey-violet in light as it decomposes.

subs.name: 硫酸钡（白色沉淀）
subs.note: 不溶于酸；医疗上服下的「钡餐」用的就是它。
subs.noteEn: Inert to acid; the same compound is swallowed as a barium meal.

subs.name: 水
subs.note: 在离子方程式里写成分子，不拆。
subs.noteEn: Written as a molecule in ionic equations, never split.

subs.name: 二氧化碳（气体）
subs.note: 接着通入澄清石灰水让它变浑，才算把碳酸根坐实。
subs.noteEn: Passed on into limewater to cloud it, which is what closes the carbonate case.

subs.name: 氨气
subs.note: 中学里常见的碱性气体，使湿润的红色石蕊试纸变蓝。
subs.noteEn: The alkaline gas of the school lab: it blues moist red litmus.

subs.name: 硫氰化铁（血红色）
subs.note: 可逆反应的产物，加 NaOH 或铁粉都能把红色弄回去。
subs.noteEn: Product of an equilibrium; either hydroxide or iron filings can pull the red back out.

subs.name: 稀硝酸（酸化用）
subs.note: 排除 CO₃²⁻、PO₄³⁻ 干扰：它们的银盐溶于酸，AgCl 不溶。
subs.noteEn: Clears carbonate and phosphate interference: their silver salts dissolve in acid, AgCl does not.

subs.name: 氯化钡溶液
subs.note: 提供 Ba²⁺；带进来的 Cl⁻ 不参与反应。
subs.noteEn: Supplies the barium; the chloride riding along is a spectator.

oneLiner: Cl⁻ 看银、SO₄²⁻ 看钡、CO₃²⁻ 放气、NH₄⁺ 变氨、Fe³⁺ 遇 SCN⁻ 血红。
oneLinerEn: Chloride meets silver, sulfate meets barium, carbonate gives off gas, ammonium gives off ammonia, iron(III) turns blood-red with thiocyanate.

eq.cond: 滴加 AgNO₃ 与稀硝酸
先稀盐酸酸化，再加 BaCl₂
eq.condEn: acidify with HCl, then barium chloride

eq.cond: 稀盐酸，气体通入石灰水
先加 KSCN 不显色，再加氯水
eq.condEn: no colour with KSCN, then chlorine water

detail: 检验的三条规矩。第一，取样分装，绝不往原试剂瓶里直接倒试剂，免得整瓶药品被污染。第二，先酸化再加沉淀剂，而且酸化用的酸要选对：检 SO₄²⁻ 用盐酸而不是硝酸，因为硝酸会把 SO₃²⁻ 氧化成 SO₄²⁻，凭空造出一堆白色沉淀；检 Cl⁻ 却必须用硝酸，因为碳酸银、磷酸银都溶于酸而 AgCl 不溶。第三，现象与结论分开写：“产生不溶于稀硝酸的白色沉淀”是现象，“溶液里有 SO₄²⁻”才是结论。还要记住顺序：证明 Fe²⁺ 必须先加 KSCN 不显色、再加氯水才变红，一上来就加氯水就分不清原液里到底是二价还是三价；NH₄⁺ 只有浓碱并加热才逸得出氨，常温稀碱几乎闻不到味道。
detailEn: Three rules of the test. First, take a sample: never pour reagent into the stock bottle, or the whole supply is spoiled. Second, acidify before precipitating, and pick the right acid — hydrochloric for sulfate, never nitric, because nitric oxidises sulfite to sulfate and manufactures a white precipitate out of nothing; but nitric for chloride, since carbonate and phosphate of silver dissolve in acid while AgCl does not. Third, keep observation and conclusion apart: 'a white precipitate insoluble in dilute nitric acid' is what you saw, 'sulfate is present' is what you claim. Order matters too: proving iron(II) means thiocyanate first with no colour, then chlorine water and the red; pour in the chlorine first and you can no longer tell which iron was in the tube. And ammonium only speaks with strong, hot alkali — cold dilute base gives off nothing worth smelling.

subs.name: 氢氧化钙（澄清石灰水）
subs.note: 检验 CO₂ 的指定试剂，变浑就算中。
subs.noteEn: The designated reagent for CO₂; cloudiness settles the case.

subs.name: 二氧化碳
subs.note: 它是碳酸盐遇酸放出的气体，也是让石灰水变浑的那一种。
subs.noteEn: The gas acids drive off carbonates, and the one that clouds limewater.

subs.name: 氨气
subs.note: 常见的碱性气体，使湿润红色石蕊试纸变蓝。
subs.noteEn: The usual alkaline gas: it blues moist red litmus.

subs.name: 氯化氢（浓盐酸发白雾）
subs.nameEn: Hydrogen chloride (the fume off concentrated hydrochloric acid)
subs.note: 与 NH₃ 相遇立刻生成固体小颗粒，看起来就是白烟。
subs.noteEn: Meets ammonia and makes solid particles at once — what the eye reads as white smoke.

subs.name: 氯气（黄绿色）
subs.note: 氧化剂，能把 I⁻ 从 KI 里拉出来；尾气要用 NaOH 吸收。
subs.noteEn: An oxidant that pulls iodide out of KI; the off-gas must be taken up by soda lye.

subs.name: 碘化钾（淀粉-KI 试纸上）
subs.note: 被氧化出的 I₂ 与淀粉一起变蓝，试纸才需要湿润。
subs.noteEn: The iodine it releases turns starch blue — which is why the paper must be damp.

subs.name: 无水硫酸铜（白色粉末）
subs.note: 专用于验水：一见水就变蓝，但不能用来干燥气体。
subs.noteEn: The water detector: blue at first sight of it, though not fit for drying gases.

subs.name: 氢气
subs.note: 点燃前必须验纯，混有空气时会爆鸣甚至炸裂容器。
subs.noteEn: Must be proved pure before lighting; mixed with air it pops and can burst the vessel.

subs.name: 氧气
subs.note: 本身不燃，但能让带火星的木条重新烧起来。
subs.noteEn: It does not burn; it relights a glowing splint instead.

subs.name: 碳酸钙（白色沉淀）
subs.note: 石灰水变浑的正是它；再通过量 CO₂ 会转成可溶的碳酸氢钙重新变清。
subs.noteEn: What clouds the limewater; pass more CO₂ and it converts to soluble calcium hydrogen carbonate, clearing again.

subs.name: 水
subs.note: 既是石灰水反应的产物，也是氢气燃烧的产物。
subs.noteEn: Product of both the limewater reaction and of burning hydrogen.

subs.name: 氯化铵（白烟）
subs.note: 固体小颗粒悬浮就是烟，不是雾；雾是液滴。
subs.noteEn: Suspended solid is smoke; suspended droplets are fog — the two are not the same word.

subs.name: 氯化钾
subs.note: 留在试纸上的可溶盐，看不出也不算现象。
subs.noteEn: A soluble salt left in the paper, seen and counted as nothing.

subs.name: 碘（单质）
subs.note: 与淀粉包合物显蓝色，这就是湿润淀粉-KI 试纸的原理。
subs.noteEn: Blue with the starch inclusion — the whole working of the moist starch-iodide paper.

subs.name: 五水硫酸铜（蓝色晶体）
subs.note: 胆矾；反过来加热到 200 ℃ 上下又变回白色。
subs.noteEn: Blue vitriol; heat it near 200 °C and it goes white again.

term: 常见气体的检验与验满
termEn: Testing Gases and Proving a Jar Is Full
oneLiner: 检验伸进瓶里，验满只在瓶口：氧复燃、CO₂ 浑石灰水、氨使石蕊变蓝。
oneLinerEn: The test goes into the jar, the fullness check stays at the mouth: oxygen relights, CO₂ clouds limewater, ammonia blues litmus.

eq.condEn: jars mouth to mouth, white fume

detail: 先把两个说法分开：检验是认气体本身，试剂要伸入瓶中；验满是证它已经集满，试纸或木条只能放在瓶口，伸进去就不算验满。逐条口径：O₂ 用带火星的木条伸入，复燃即为氧气，验满时在瓶口放一燃着木条、烧得更旺即满；CO₂ 通入澄清石灰水变浑，验满用燃着木条在瓶口火焰熄灭——但能使火焰熄灭的气体不止 CO₂，所以熄灭只说明它不支持燃烧，不能当作鉴定。NH₃ 是常见的碱性气体，使湿润的红色石蕊试纸变蓝；验满把蘸过浓盐酸的玻璃棒靠近瓶口，冒白烟即满。Cl₂ 使湿润的淀粉-KI 试纸变蓝并有刺激性，必须在通风橱里做、尾气通入 NaOH 溶液。SO₂ 使品红溶液浅色、加热后颜色又回来，这正是它与 CO₂ 的分界：CO₂ 不能让品红褪色。H₂ 点燃前必须验纯：用拇指堵住集满气体的试管口，移近火焰松开，听到尖锐爆鸣说明还混有空气，直到只留一声沉闷的“噗”才算净。
detailEn: Separate the two ideas first: identification asks what gas is there and dips the reagent inside the jar; proving the jar full only touches the mouth, and anything thrust in no longer proves fullness. Oxygen relights a glowing splint inside, and a burning splint held at the mouth burns brighter once the jar is full. Carbon dioxide clouds limewater, and a flame dies at the mouth when the jar is filled — but plenty of gases kill a flame, so going out only says 'does not support burning', never 'is CO₂'. Ammonia is the common alkaline gas and blues moist red litmus; a glass rod wetted with concentrated hydrochloric acid near the mouth shows white fume when the jar is full. Chlorine blues moist starch-iodide paper and stings, so it is worked in a fume hood with the off-gas led into soda lye. Sulfur dioxide fades fuchsin and the colour returns on warming, which is exactly where it parts from carbon dioxide — CO₂ cannot bleach fuchsin at all. Hydrogen must be proved pure before lighting: thumb over the mouth of a filled tube, bring it to the flame and release — a sharp bark means air is still mixed in, and only a soft 'puff' means it is clean.

subs.name: 汞（水银）
subs.note: 常温下唯一的液态金属，洒落后滚成小珠、难收集，蒸气有毒。
subs.noteEn: The only liquid metal at room temperature: it rolls into beads hard to gather, and its vapour is toxic.

subs.name: 硫粉
subs.note: 常温下就能与汞缓慢结合，把易挥发的汞固定下来。
subs.noteEn: Combines with mercury slowly at room temperature, pinning down what would otherwise evaporate.

subs.name: 硫化汞（固体）
subs.note: 不再挥发，可以安全扫起、密闭上交；天然矿物即辰砂。
subs.noteEn: No longer volatile, so it can be swept up, sealed and handed in; the natural mineral is cinnabar.

term: 实验基本操作与事故处理
termEn: Bench Technique and First Moves After an Accident
oneLiner: 酸入水、管不对人、pH 试纸不预先润湿；水银洒了不是用扫把，而是撒硫粉。
oneLinerEn: Acid into water, tube mouth away from people, no wetting pH paper first; spilled mercury gets sulfur dust, not a broom.
detail: 取用：固体「一斜二送三直立」，免得药品沾在管口；液体瓶塞倒放、标签向手心、瓶口挨着试管口倒。闻气味时用手轻轻扇动使少量气体飘入鼻孔，绝不能把鼻子凑到瓶口。加热：试管里液体不超过容积的三分之一，管口不对人，先均匀预热再固定；加热固体时管口略向下，免得冷凝水倒流炸裂试管。计量：托盘天平左物右码，腐蚀性药品放在玻璃器皿里称；量筒只读体积，不能加热、不作反应容器、也不在里面溶解东西。分离：过滤记「一贴二低三靠」，蒸发结晶到大量晶体析出就停火、用余热蒸干。稀释：浓硫酸只能沿器壁缓缓注入水里并不断搅拌，反过来会因局部沸腾把酸液溅到身上。试纸：pH 试纸不能预先润湿（润湿等于把待测液稀释），而石蕊试纸、淀粉-KI 试纸必须用蒸馏水润湿。气密性：先把导管口插进水里再用手捂住容器，管口连续冒气泡、松手后水柱回升才算不漏。善后：钠、钾等活泼金属残渣用乙醇慢慢处理，不丢入废液缸；含银、钡、重金属的废液要回收，不随意倒掉。
detailEn: Handling: for solids, tilt, deliver upright, straighten, so nothing sticks at the mouth; for liquids, stopper upside-down on the bench, label to the palm, mouth to mouth. Waft the gas toward your nose with a hand — never put your nose at the bottle. Heating: no more than a third of the tube with liquid, mouth pointed at nobody, warm the whole tube before fixing one spot; when heating a solid the mouth tips slightly down so condensate cannot run back and crack the tube. Weighing: substance left, weights right, corrosives always in glass rather than on the pan; a measuring cylinder reads volume only — it is not heated, not a reaction vessel, not a beaker for dissolving. Separation: filter by 'one paste, two lows, three rests', and stop an evaporation while plenty of crystals still form, letting residual heat dry it. Dilution: concentrated sulfuric acid goes down the wall into water with stirring, never the other way, since the local boil throws acid. Paper: pH paper must stay dry, because wetting it dilutes the sample, while litmus and starch-iodide paper must be wetted first. Leaks: stand the delivery tube in water and warm the flask in your hands — a steady line of bubbles, and water climbing back when you let go, is what tight looks like. Cleanup: sodium and potassium scraps are destroyed with ethanol, never dropped in the waste jar, and silver, barium and heavy-metal wastes are collected rather than poured out.

term: 常用仪器的精度与加热口径
termEn: Glassware: Precision and What May Be Heated
oneLiner: 量筒读到 0.1 mL、滴定管读到 0.01 mL；量器一律不加热、不作反应容器。
oneLinerEn: A cylinder reads to 0.1 mL, a burette to 0.01; measuring glassware is never heated and never a reaction vessel.
detail: 认仪器先认三件事：能量到多小、能不能加热、能不能当反应容器。量器类是后两条禁令的共同答案：量筒、容量瓶、酸式与碱式滴定管、漏斗一律不能加热，也不作反应容器、不在里面溶解或稀释——受热会让刻度失准，受热不均还会裂。精度口径要背准：托盘天平读到 0.1 g，量筒读到 0.1 mL（用 10 mL 量筒量 9.5 mL 可以，写 9.50 mL 就不行），滴定管读到 0.01 mL（所以滴定终点记作 22.60 mL 而不是 22.6 mL），容量瓶只有一条标线，只能配它标定的那种体积。读数时视线与凹液面最低处水平：俯视使量筒读数偏大、实际量到的偏少，仰视恰好相反。磨口与塞子也有讲究：碱液会把玻璃里的二氧化硅慢慢变成有黏性的硅酸钠，把磨口塞粘死，所以盛碱液用橡胶塞而不是玻璃塞。温度计的位置随用途改：测液体温度插进液面以下、不碰底也不碰壁，蒸馏时水银球要跟支管口齐平，因为那时要读的是蒸气的温度。pH 试纸不能预先润湿（润湿等于把待测液稀释），石蕊试纸与淀粉-KI 试纸却必须润湿——差别在于前者测浓度、后者测气体能不能与它反应。人教版新教材已把「石棉网」改叫「陶土网」，两者作用一样：让玻璃仪器受热均匀。
detailEn: Every piece of glassware answers three questions: how finely it measures, whether it can be heated, and whether it can serve as a reaction vessel. The measuring class settles the last two together — cylinders, volumetric flasks, burettes and funnels take no heat, host no reaction, and dissolve nothing in place, since warmth moves the very volume their graduations were calibrated for and uneven heating cracks the glass. Know the precisions by heart: a tray balance to 0.1 g, a cylinder to 0.1 mL (a 10 mL cylinder can deliver 9.5 mL but never 9.50), a burette to 0.01 mL (which is why an endpoint is recorded as 22.60 mL, not 22.6), and a volumetric flask carries a single mark for the one volume it was made for. Read at eye level against the bottom of the meniscus: looking down over-reads a cylinder and leaves you short, looking up does the reverse. Ground glass and stoppers follow chemistry too — alkali slowly turns the silica in the joint into sticky sodium silicate, welding stopper to neck, so alkaline solutions get rubber rather than glass. Where the thermometer goes depends on the job: into the liquid but clear of base and wall when you measure the liquid, level with the side arm in distillation, because there you want the vapour's temperature. pH paper must stay dry, since wetting it dilutes the sample, while litmus and starch-iodide paper must be wetted — the first measures a concentration, the second asks whether a gas reacts with it. Newer Chinese textbooks say clay-centred wire gauze where older ones said asbestos; the purpose, even heating, is unchanged.

term: 分离与提纯的方法及仪器配套
termEn: Separation and Purification: Method Matched to Apparatus
oneLiner: 不溶靠过滤、可溶靠蒸发、沸点差靠蒸馏、溶解度差靠萃取——先看靠什么分开。
oneLinerEn: Insoluble goes by filtering, dissolved by evaporating, a boiling gap by distillation, a solubility gap by extraction — first ask what holds them apart.
detail: 分离提纯的选法只看一件事：混合物靠什么性质分得开。不溶固体对液体用过滤，记「一贴二低三靠」：滤纸紧贴漏斗内壁，滤纸边缘低于漏斗口、液面低于滤纸边缘，烧杯紧靠玻璃棒、玻璃棒下端靠在三层滤纸一侧、漏斗尖嘴靠接收烧杯内壁；玻璃棒在这里是引流，不是搅拌。洗沉淀的办法是往漏斗里加蒸馏水至浸没沉淀，等水自然流下再重复两三次。可溶固体从溶液里取出用蒸发结晶：蒸发皿直接加热，玻璃棒搅动防局部过热造成液滴飞溅，出现大量晶体就停火、用余热蒸干。但带结晶水的、受热会分解或会水解的一律不能蒸干，要改蒸发浓缩、降温结晶：NaHCO₃ 受热就放 CO₂，FeCl₃ 溶液蒸到最后只会得到氧化铁而得不到无水氯化铁。互溶的液体看沸点差用蒸馏：加碎瓷片防暴沸，忘了加必须等液体冷下来再补，温度计水银球跟支管口齐平（读的是蒸气温度），冷却水下口进上口出，让冷凝管始终充水且与水蒸气逆流换热，先通水后加热。溶质在两相里溶解度差得远用萃取分液，萃取剂三条要求：与原溶剂互不相溶、溶质在其中溶解度大、与溶质不反应；四氯化碳从碘水里萃取碘，下层紫红色从下口放出，上层水层从上口倒出，分液漏斗用前要检漏、振荡时要倒转过来适时旋开活塞放气。气体除杂走洗气瓶，长管进短管出，让气体鼓泡通过洗涤液；干燥管则是大孔进小孔出。还有两处易混：淀粉胶体里混了小分子离子，靠半透膜渗析除去，碘里混了沙用升华——但氯化铵看起来会「升华」其实是受热分解成氨与氯化氢、在冷处又化合回来，所以不能用升华法把它和碘分开。
detailEn: One question decides the method: what property holds the mixture apart. Insoluble solid from liquid goes through a filter, remembered as 'one paste, two lows, three rests' — paper wetted flat to the funnel wall, paper below the rim and liquid below the paper edge, beaker to the rod, rod to the three-ply side, nozzle to the receiving wall; the rod guides the liquid here and does not stir. A precipitate is washed by filling the funnel with distilled water until the solid is covered, letting it drain, and repeating two or three times. A dissolved solid comes back by evaporation: the dish goes straight on the flame, the rod keeps things moving so nothing boils locally and spits, and the heat goes off while plenty of crystals are still forming, residual heat doing the drying. Anything carrying water of crystallisation, decomposing on heating or hydrolysing must not be dried out — sodium hydrogen carbonate gives up CO₂, and an iron(III) chloride solution evaporated to dryness leaves iron oxide, never anhydrous iron(III) chloride. Miscible liquids separate on boiling point in a distillation: anti-bumping chips, and if you forgot them, add them only once the liquid is cold; the thermometer bulb level with the side arm, because it reads vapour; cooling water in at the lower port and out at the upper so the jacket stays full and works counter-current, water on before the flame. Where the solute prefers one of two immiscible phases, extract and separate: the extractant must not mix with the original solvent, must dissolve the solute far better, and must not react with it — carbon tetrachloride pulls iodine out of water, and the violet lower layer is run off through the tap while the upper aqueous layer is poured off the top; the separatory funnel is leak-checked first and vented at the neck during shaking. Gas impurities wash out through a bubbler, in the long tube and out the short, while a drying tube takes the wide end first. Two last confusions: ions are dialysed away from starch colloid through a semi-permeable membrane, and iodine is sublimed from sand — but ammonium chloride only imitates sublimation, splitting into ammonia and hydrogen chloride and recombining in a cold spot, which is why sublimation cannot part it from iodine.

subs.name: 二氧化硅（玻璃的主体）
subs.note: 磨口塞、试剂瓶、量器都靠它，但它能被碱和氢氟酸侵蚀。
subs.noteEn: Stoppers, bottles and glassware are built on it, yet alkali and hydrofluoric acid both attack it.

subs.name: 氢氧化钠（碱液）
subs.note: 长期接触磨口就会把塞子粘住，所以碱液瓶配橡胶塞。
subs.noteEn: Long contact with a ground joint welds it shut, hence the rubber stopper on alkali bottles.

subs.name: 硅酸钠（有黏性）
subs.note: 就是它把玻璃塞与瓶口粘成一体，也是水玻璃的主要成分。
subs.noteEn: This is what cements stopper to neck, and the main ingredient of water glass.

subs.name: 水
subs.note: 两个侵蚀反应的共同产物。
subs.noteEn: A product of both attack reactions.

subs.name: 氢氟酸（不能碰玻璃）
subs.note: 能直接咬玻璃，只能装在塑料瓶里；刻玻璃字用的就是它。
subs.noteEn: It eats glass outright, so it lives in plastic; it is also what etches glass.

subs.name: 四氟化硅（气体）
subs.note: 玻璃被氢氟酸腐蚀后的硅去向。
subs.noteEn: Where the silicon goes when hydrofluoric acid works on glass.

subs.name: 硝酸银（见光分解）
subs.note: 棕色瓶里的常客，瓶壁内侧那层灰黑就是分解出的银。
subs.noteEn: A regular of the amber shelf; the grey film inside such bottles is the silver it shed.

subs.name: 银（单质，黑灰色）
subs.note: 分解产物，附在瓶壁上使旧瓶发黑。
subs.noteEn: Its decomposition product, which darkens an old bottle from inside.

subs.name: 二氧化氮
subs.note: 浓硝酸、硝酸银分解都有它；红棕色、有毒。
subs.noteEn: Fumed from nitric acid and from silver nitrate alike; red-brown and toxic.

subs.name: 氧气
subs.note: 硝酸盐分解放出的气体，也是氧化剂自身被还原的证据。
subs.noteEn: The gas a nitrate gives up, and the mark that the oxidiser reduced itself.

term: 药品的存放与容器选择
termEn: Storing Reagents and Choosing the Container
oneLiner: 怕空气的泡煤油、怕水的密封、怕光的进棕色瓶、怕玻璃的换塑料瓶。
oneLinerEn: What fears air keeps in paraffin, what fears water stays sealed, what fears light takes the amber bottle, what fears glass moves to plastic.

eq.cond: 磨口处玻璃被碱缓慢侵蚀

detail: 药品怎么存，只看它跟什么反应：跟空气反应的隔空气，跟水反应的隔水，见光分解的躲光，跟玻璃反应的换塑料。钠、钾泡在煤油里（它密度比煤油大，沉在下面刚好隔绝空气和水），白磷浸在冷水中（着火点只有约 40 ℃，而它不与水反应），液溴上面加一层水封——溴密度大、只能微溶于水，那层水能压住挥发。见光分解的三类必放棕色瓶：硝酸银、浓硝酸、氯水；硝酸银分解会析出单质银，所以旧瓶内壁常带一层灰黑。磨口塞看酸碱性：碱液（NaOH、Na₂CO₃）会缓慢侵蚀玻璃磨口、生成有黏性的硅酸钠，把塞子和瓶口粘成一体，所以碱液瓶用橡胶塞，装碱液的滴定管也必须用碱式（橡胶管里嵌玻璃珠）而不能用带玻璃磨口活塞的酸式；氢氟酸更彻底，它直接和二氧化硅反应，只能装塑料瓶。亚铁盐溶液里放一枚铁钉，把已经氧化出来的 Fe³⁺ 又还原回去，能顶住一阵子。无水硫酸铜、氯化钙这类干燥剂和易潮解的药品放干燥器。存放还要看相容：氧化剂（高锰酸钾、硝酸盐）不能与有机物、还原剂同橱，酸与碱分开，钠钾远离水与酸。
detailEn: Storage asks one question: what does this reagent react with. What fears air is cut off from it, what fears water from that, what fears light from the light, what fears glass gets a different bottle. Sodium and potassium sit under paraffin — denser than the oil, they sink and are sealed from both air and moisture; white phosphorus lies under cold water, since it ignites near 40 °C but does not react with water; bromine keeps a water seal on top, being heavy and only slightly soluble, so the layer above it damps the fuming. Three light-sensitive regulars demand amber glass — silver nitrate, concentrated nitric acid, chlorine water — and since silver nitrate breaks down to the metal, an old bottle greys from the inside. Stoppers follow acid-base chemistry: alkali (sodium hydroxide, sodium carbonate) slowly eats the ground joint into sticky sodium silicate and welds stopper to neck, so alkaline solutions get rubber, and a burette for them uses the bead-and-tube pattern rather than a glass tap; hydrofluoric acid is more thorough still, reacting with the silica itself, and can only live in plastic. An iron nail in an iron(II) salt solution reduces back the iron(III) that has already formed and buys time. Desiccants and deliquescent solids — anhydrous copper sulfate, calcium chloride — keep to a desiccator. Compatibility decides the shelf as well: oxidisers such as permanganate and the nitrates are not stored with organics or reducers, acids apart from bases, sodium and potassium far from both water and acid.
